bullets.title: June CPI Delivers Major Dovish Surprise; July Hike Odds Collapse to Near Zero
bullets.body: Headline CPI fell -0.42% m/m (largest monthly drop since April 2020), driven by a 9.7% decline in gasoline and -5.7% energy. Core CPI came in at -0.02% m/m vs. +0.22% consensus, with core services ex-housing at -0.21% and shelter rising just 0.1% m/m (weakest since Jan 2021). July Fed rate hike odds collapsed from ~40-50% to 4bps priced by market; 2-year Treasury yields fell >10bps. Core PCE preliminarily tracking ~0.15-0.2% m/m—'okish, not great'—leaving September cut in play but July firmly off the table.

bullets.title: Fed Chair Warsh Emphasizes Inflation Over Labor, Challenges Trimmed Mean Credibility
bullets.body: Warsh's economic framework has shifted decisively toward inflation reduction, arguing the Fed must prioritize price stability when labor is near full employment. He critiqued the Trimmed Mean CPI as 'deeply misleading' when monthly price changes skew positive. Warsh flagged the balance sheet's liability side (reserve regime) as more relevant than assets, and expressed openness to abandoning the dot plot. Separately, a Fedspeak model shows hawkish positioning at its highest since November 2023 ahead of his congressional testimony—though today's CPI data materially softened that impulse.

bullets.title: IBM -20%+ Pre-Announcement: Capex Reprioritization Signals Enterprise IT Rotation into Hardware
bullets.body: IBM reported preliminary Q2 revenue of $17.2B vs. $17.86B est. (EPS $2.27 vs. $3.02 est.), with CEO Arvind Krishna citing unexpected client capex shifts toward servers, storage, and memory ahead of anticipated price increases—away from mainframe (Z-series, -7% infrastructure) and related software (+5% vs. 10-11% expected). Large deal slippage in late June was a key driver. JPMorgan views the capex reprioritization as a positive read-through for cybersecurity vendors (PANW, CRWD, ZS) and server/storage names (DELL, MU, STX, WDC), while enterprise software broadly (NOW, CRM, INTU, ACN) is under pressure. Citi views the miss as idiosyncratic to IBM rather than a broad enterprise spending issue.

bullets.title: Big Bank Earnings: GS and BAC Beat Massively on Equities Trading; JPM Drops Despite Record Profit
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs blew out estimates: equities S&T $7.42B vs. $5.02B est., FICC $4.59B vs. $3.76B est., investment banking $3.40B vs. $2.88B est. BofA also beat: equities S&T $3.62B vs. $2.69B est., total revenue $31.56B vs. $30.39B est. JPM reported EPS $7.70 vs. $5.58 est. with equities $6.03B crushing the $3.98B estimate, but stock fell as market focused on forward NII guidance. Wells Fargo beat on fees and credit but rising deposit costs (1.99% vs. 1.91% est.) pressured NIM trajectory.

bullets.title: Geopolitical Escalation: US Strikes Iranian Oil Infrastructure; Brent Crude +5% to $87.49
bullets.body: Reports of US strikes on Abadan and Imam Khomeini Port in Iran drove Brent crude up 5% to $87.49/bbl, its highest level since June 12. Explosions were also reported near Bandar Abbas/Bushehr. The IRGC disabled two supertankers in the Persian Gulf. Trump is reportedly 'very serious' about a 20% fee plan for Strait of Hormuz transit (potential ~$100M+/day revenue if applied to dark fleet). The UK called for toll-free Hormuz reopening while Iran threatened Elon Musk's Middle East operations including Starlink. Bond market volatility (MOVE) spiked alongside oil.

bullets.title: Hedge Fund Positioning: Tech Hardware/Semis See Largest Week of Buying on Record After Heavy Unwind
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reports hedge funds were net buyers of global equities last week, with Tech Hardware and Semis registering the largest single week of buying on record—approximately 30% buyback of previously unwound AI exposure. Despite this, HF net leverage remains near 12-month lows and L/S ratio for semis/hardware sits at 12-month lows with 75% of US mutual funds underweight semis vs. benchmark. Retail single-stock net buying fell to its lowest weekly level since Covid; Mag 7 is no longer trading as a unified retail position.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley Raises Hyperscale Capex to ~$1.4T by 2028; Memory Shortage 'Durable Through 2030+'
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised hyperscale capex forecasts to ~$1.2T in 2027 and ~$1.4T in 2028, with total AI compute capacity growing ~4x from 2025–2028. New cost-per-GW math supports upward revisions for META, AMZN, and GOOGL. Separately, MS QDS notes NVDA and SK Hynix CEOs confirmed memory constraints durable beyond 2030, with GPU rental rates up 5-10% in July. Anthropic daily ARR additions accelerated m/m in June.

bullets.title: NY Becomes First US State to Ban Large Data Center Construction for Up to One Year
bullets.body: New York Governor Hochul enacted an executive order freezing environmental permits for data centers with 50MW+ electricity loads for up to one year while the state develops a regulatory framework. Citi maintains Buy on WULF (Lake Mariner unaffected; Cayuga contingent on local not state permits), EQIX (top pick), and DLR. The moratorium is being watched as a potential template for other states; ~$156B of data center projects were cancelled/delayed in 2025 and ~$130B in 1Q26 nationally from similar regulatory headwinds.

bullets.title: US Grants AI Chip Licenses to Chinese Firms ZTE, Kingsoft; Signals Export Restriction Easing
bullets.body: The US granted export licenses to ZTE, Kingsoft, and Maginfra to purchase NVIDIA H200 and AMD AI chips, signaling a potential easing of AI chip export restrictions to China. Separately, Jefferies raised its China AI capex forecast 23% to $1 trillion cumulatively through 2030, with China expected to purchase 300K H200 chips in 2026 as inference demand surges.

bullets.title: NFIB Small Business Optimism Surges to 97.4 in June; CEO Confidence Also Improving
bullets.body: NFIB Small Business Optimism rose to 97.4 in June vs. 95.7 consensus and 95.3 prior, reaching its highest level since February and marking the first increase in outlook expectations this year. The share of owners expecting better business conditions jumped to 10% from 3%. Separately, a Chief Executive Group survey showed nearly 50% of CEOs report demand higher than a year ago. Consumer cyclical ETFs saw the largest inflows for the week ended 7/10 while US large-cap ETFs reversed to the largest outflows.

bullets.title: ASML Faces 'Magic Number' Bar for Tomorrow's Print; Elevated Multiple Raises De-Rating Risk
bullets.body: Jefferies flags ASML must guide for at least 90 low-NA EUV systems shipped to support the stock; anything below triggers declines. The stock currently trades at 50x FY26 / 38x FY27 consensus EPS after a 66% re-rating since September 2025. De-rating risk factors include MATCH Act threat to China sales (20-30% decline; 20% of sales), revenue recognition timing mismatches (ships in 2027 may not be recognized until 2028), and hyperscaler capex sustainability concerns. Historical precedent: ASML de-rated 29% in 2018, 47% in 2021-22, 45% in 2024-25.

bullets.title: MSFT Down 2.8% Premarket in IBM Sympathy; Enterprise Software Broadly Lower
bullets.body: Microsoft fell 2.8% premarket following IBM's miss, part of a broad enterprise software selloff: ADBE -5.6%, INTU -7.3%, NOW -8.1%, CRM, SNOW, MDB, PLTR all down 5%+. The read-through debate centers on whether IBM's shortfall is idiosyncratic (JPM, Citi view) or signals a broader enterprise IT spending rotation away from software toward hardware infrastructure.

bullets.title: Momentum Factor Volatility Exceptionally High; High Beta Momentum Basket Down 21.5% in One Month
bullets.body: The momentum factor's volatility is running exceptionally high relative to broader market volatility per market commentary. Hedgeye reports the High Beta Momentum basket is down 6% on the day and -21.5% over the past month; the Retail Sentiment basket is down -10.3% in the past month. SOXL's 3x leverage rebalancing forced >$6.5B in semiconductor selling during the recent correction, amplifying sector drawdowns.

bullets.title: Oil Market Regime: Hedgeye Flags Quad3 'Oil Reflation' Pattern; WTI Breaks Above $76.59 Signal
bullets.body: Hedgeye's macro framework places the US in Quad4 for Q3 2026 but flags August shifts to monthly Quad3 Reflation/Stagflation. WTI broke above its $76.59 TRADE Signal resistance, establishing a bullish short-term trade pattern (Risk Range $65-82) while the longer-term trend remains bearish. EU/UK gas is separately being flagged as a larger reflation risk than gasoline. UST 2-year yield hit a new cycle high at 4.29%.

bullets.title: Tower Semiconductor +19% Premarket on ~$3B Japanese Government Investment
bullets.body: Tower Semiconductor surged 18.6-19.7% premarket after announcing approximately $3 billion in investment from the Japanese government, focused on silicon photonics and germanium capacity expansion.

bullets.title: Global IPOs Up 125% YoY in 2Q26; Tender Offers Dominant Liquidity Event for Private Co's
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's founder survey notes global IPOs are up 125% year-over-year in 2Q26, including SpaceX's record-breaking IPO in June. Tender offers have emerged as the most-used structured liquidity event for private companies, with 54% having conducted one previously and 47% planning one as their next liquidity event. 95% of founders identify AI as critical to business success but fewer than 25% feel well-supported in keeping pace.

bullets.title: SK Hynix Slashing Capacity Expansion Plans to ~1/6 of Original Targets by 2028
bullets.body: Reports indicate SK Hynix may add only roughly one-sixth of its planned new memory capacity by 2028, signaling either significant capital discipline or demand uncertainty in the memory market. This contrasts with Citi's bullish view on Korean memory fundamentals where DRAM/NAND ASPs are projected +234%/+236% YoY for 2026E and HBM pricing is forecast to grow 70% YoY in 2027E.

bullets.title: DeepSeek in Preliminary Talks for New Funding Round at ~$71B Valuation
bullets.body: DeepSeek is in preliminary discussions with new investors for an additional funding round that would value the Chinese AI lab at approximately $71 billion pre-deal, per FT. One observer believes the company is worth at least $150B. This development reinforces the competitive pressure from Chinese open-source AI models on Western incumbents.

bullets.title: NY Data Center Moratorium and Hormuz Risk Drive Cross-Asset Volatility; VIX at 16.40
bullets.body: VIX is at 16.40 (+4.4%) with S&P 500 +0.5% to 7,549.96. The tape is navigating simultaneous shocks: IBM's miss hitting enterprise software, Hormuz/Iran escalation spiking oil and bond vol (MOVE), NY data center moratorium weighing on infrastructure names, and a dovish CPI providing an offsetting bid. UK 10-year gilt yield broke above 5% on oil/fiscal concerns.
